summary: HIGH-PRIORITY verification pass focused on the reported skill-tree zoom crash regression. CRITICAL RESULT: crash is NOT reproducible. Performed multiple aggressive stress rounds on the live Skill Tree canvas: 30 rapid alternating wheel ticks (15ms apart), a combined drag+zoom gesture (20 simultaneous mouse-move+wheel steps), and an EXTREME round of 60 near-zero-delay wheel ticks — all with a framenavigated listener attached to detect any reload. Zero navigation events fired, skill-tree DOM stayed mounted/interactive the entire time, no console/page errors, and SP/save state was untouched after the stress (confirms no app restart). Also confirmed: Camp sidebar now shows '⚡ N ATTR' (data-testid=camp-attr-points) in the currency list, and clicking it correctly opens the Character panel showing the ATTRIBUTES section (Attack/Dexterity/Vitality/Mobility/Intelligence/Elemental/Magic with +points free counter). Fired the starter hydropistol during a live tutorial run: muzzle-flash light around the player appears blended (whitish-blue, not pure saturated blue) and the projectile bolt renders as a small dot consistent with the described 50% size reduction; no visual glitches or console/shader errors during firing. Full regression: character creation -> tutorial run -> movement -> firing all worked without crashes across ~8 fresh sessions.

ui_bugs.issue: Minor flakiness observed across sessions: sometimes the 'tap/click to continue' dialogue (shown both at first load and again as a pre-run cutscene after clicking welcome-fight) required 5-8 clicks/spacebar presses over several seconds to fully dismiss, occasionally appearing to not respond to a single click immediately after page load. Not related to the skill-tree bug and did not block any flow, but noted as a UX rough edge worth a quick look if reported by users.

action_items: None required for the critical zoom-crash fix — verified genuinely fixed under aggressive stress. Optional/low-priority: investigate minor intro-dialogue click responsiveness flakiness noted above if it resurfaces in user reports.
critical_code_review_comments: CONFIRMED FIX: SkillTree.jsx's rAF-throttled wheelPending ref + CSS style={transform} (line 180, instead of the SVG transform attribute) fully eliminates the crash — verified via live stress testing (110+ wheel events across 3 rounds, plus combined drag+zoom), not just code review. No reload/navigation events detected via a framenavigated listener.
GOOD: Camp.jsx attrFreePts computation and camp-attr-points currency line render and click-through to CharacterPanel work correctly end-to-end.
GOOD: pixiRenderer.js lighting changes (mixHex blend, smaller hydropistol bolt) visually consistent with described fix; no shader/GlProgram console errors seen in any session.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% - critical zoom-crash regression confirmed FIXED (top priority), attr-points indicator + character panel flow confirmed working, lighting changes visually plausible and error-free. XP orb glow specifically was not caught in a screenshot mid-kill (short session budget) but zero shader/console errors were observed across all sessions including gameplay, which is the primary risk area.

success_rate.context_for_next_testing_agent: TOP PRIORITY ITEM (skill-tree zoom crash) IS CONFIRMED FIXED via live aggressive stress testing, not just code review - this can be communicated to the user with confidence. If a future pass wants to close the one remaining minor gap: catch a kill + big XP orb pickup mid-run and screenshot to visually confirm the new shader-based orb glow (_xpOrbLitPool) renders correctly - budget/time did not allow reaching a kill this pass, but zero GlProgram/shader console errors were observed throughout, which is the main risk indicator for that change.
success_rate.rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: SVG 'transform' XML attribute on the zoomable <g> (containing ~65 nodes + blur filters) forced full filter-region recompute on every wheel event, and un-throttled setState calls (up to 20+/sec during a fast scroll) compounded this into a tab freeze/crash. Fix applied: CSS style={transform} (GPU-composited, skips filter recompute) + requestAnimationFrame throttling (max 1 state update per frame). Verified fixed by reproducing the exact aggressive-scroll conditions described by the user (15-20+ ticks/sec, sustained for seconds, plus combined drag) with zero crashes/reloads across 3 separate stress rounds.
